a Claude call tells a refusal from an unreadable output in process
summary: in-process-workers.test.ts now proves a refusal (claude/result-turn-limit, a real capture of `claude -p --output-format json --max-turns 1 'Run the shell command date with your Bash tool and tell me its output.'`, exit 1, error_max_turns) and an unreadable output (claude/result-text) complete apart in process, with distinct executions and exit codes. ScriptedClaude.#played no longer assumes its capture's stdout is JSON: it tries to parse it and, on failure, replays the capture unchanged instead of throwing, which is what let the text capture reach the worker as an unparsable stream. Kept the fix to a plain try/catch around JSON.parse rather than also rejecting a parsed non-object (e.g. a bare array), since no real claude capture ever produces one and the extra branch would have been an unreachable check with no test to justify it.
